title: What can we read from the ordered shoe sizes?
description: A question from the book gives the shoe sizes of twenty seven students in ascending order. The video reads the largest and smallest sizes, counts one block, and adds three blocks.
teaching_notes: One idea: in an ordered list, the ends give the smallest and largest values and equal values sit in one block. Watch for children who count the different sizes instead of the students, or who include size four in 'larger than 4'.

source: Figure it Out: the largest, the smallest and the counts from the ordered shoe sizes
video_script.why: The child reads facts from an ordered list: the two ends, one block, and a sum of blocks.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own shoe-size data
video_script.payoff_line: Fifteen students wear sizes larger than four.

final_answer.spoken: the largest size is seven, the smallest size is three, ten students wear size five, and fifteen students wear sizes larger than four

names.{{NAME_6}}: teacher who recorded the shoe sizes of her students

never_show: the 27 sizes in the jumbled grid
maths_rules: Counting the grid: size 3 occurs 3 times, size 4 occurs 9 times, size 5 occurs 10 times, size 6 occurs 4 times, size 7 occurs 1 time.
video_script.design: The ordered row of 27 sizes on the left, split into five blocks; the question parts a to d on the right.

beats.on_screen: title card with a teacher and a long row of shoe sizes in ascending order, from 3 at the left to 7 at the right

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the teacher
marks.order: the long ordered row slides across the board
marks.ask: a question mark lights up above the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the shoe sizes noted by {{NAME_6}}.
<bookmark mark='order'/>She has arranged all twenty seven sizes in ascending order.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What can we read from this ordered list?

beats.on_screen: the ordered row and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: an ordered row with its first entry marked smallest and its last entry marked largest, and equal sizes boxed together

marks.ends: the first and last entries of the row are marked
marks.blocks: the equal sizes are boxed into blocks

narration: <bookmark mark='ends'/>In an ordered list, the first entry is the smallest and the last entry is the largest.
<bookmark mark='blocks'/>Equal sizes sit together, so each block can be counted at once.

beats.on_screen: Given: 27 students in ascending order: size 3 occurs 3 times, size 4 occurs 9 times, size 5 occurs 10 times, size 6 occurs 4 times, size 7 occurs 1 time

marks.given: the ordered list is written as the given
marks.low: the blocks of sizes three and four are marked
marks.high: the blocks of sizes five, six and seven are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the ordered sizes of twenty seven students.
<bookmark mark='low'/>Size three occurs three times, and size four occurs nine times.
<bookmark mark='high'/>Size five occurs ten times, size six four times, and size seven once.

beats.on_screen: To find: a. the largest size, b. the smallest size, c. students in size 5, d. students in sizes larger than 4

marks.find: the four lines to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the largest size, the smallest size, and two counts.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the first entry is 3, the smallest; the last entry is 7, the largest

marks.ends: the first and last entries of the row are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='ends'/>Step one, look at the two ends of the ordered list.
The first entry is three, and the last entry is seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the block of 5s has 10 entries, so 10 students wear size 5

marks.five: the block of size five is boxed and its entries are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step two, find the block of size five.
It has ten entries, so ten students wear size five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: sizes larger than 4 are 5, 6 and 7: 10 + 4 + 1 = 15

marks.larger: the blocks of sizes five, six and seven are joined and added

narration: <bookmark mark='larger'/>Step three, the sizes larger than four are five, six and seven.
Their blocks have ten, four and one entries, which make fifteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check all the blocks: 3 + 9 + 10 + 4 + 1 = 27 students

marks.check: all five blocks are added in a line under the list

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, add all five blocks to check the list.
Three, nine, ten, four and one make twenty seven.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a. largest size 7; b. smallest size 3; c. size 5: 10 students; d. larger than 4: 15 students
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The largest size is seven, and the smallest size is three.
Ten students wear size five.
Fifteen students wear sizes larger than four.
